title: Atrial fibrillation: type, history and anticoagulation
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's atrial fibrillation and related long-term drug therapy.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for history of atrial fibrillation.

HPI
The patient is a 52-year-old male presenting for a routine follow-up regarding his history of atrial fibrillation. He originally underwent a catheter ablation procedure several years ago to manage his arrhythmia. He reports that he has had no recurrence since the procedure and feels well. He denies any palpitations, shortness of breath, dizziness, or syncope. Because he has remained stable and asymptomatic, he is not currently taking any medication for rate or rhythm control. He also confirms that he does not require any medication for his heart condition at this time.

Medication List
Multivitamin daily.
Lisinopril 10mg daily.

Vitals
BP: 122/78 mmHg
HR: 74 bpm (regular)
Temp: 98.6 F
RR: 16 breaths/min
SpO2: 98% on room air

Recent Labs
eGFR: 88 mL/min/1.73m2
HbA1c: 5.6%
TSH: 2.1 mIU/L
Potassium: 4.2 mEq/L

Review of Systems
The patient denies chest pain, shortness of breath, fever, chills, weight changes, or polyuria. He denies any neurological deficits or changes in vision.

Social History
The patient works as a software engineer. He reports exercising three times a week and non-smoking status. He drinks one to two alcoholic beverages on weekends.

Family History
Father: Hypertension, myocardial infarction at age 65.
Mother: Type 2 diabetes, deceased at age 78.
Siblings: One brother with hypertension.

Exam
General: Well-appearing, alert, and in no acute distress.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm. S1, S2 heard clearly. No murmurs, rubs, or gallops noted. Capillary refill is less than 2 seconds.
Respiratory: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Neurological: Alert and oriented x3. Cranial nerves intact. No focal weakness or sensory loss.

Assessment
1. Atrial fibrillation, status post ablation. The patient is clinically stable with no recurrence since the procedure. He remains at low risk for complications and does not require any medication for rhythm or rate management.

Plan
1. Continue current monitoring.
2. Follow up in 12 months for routine evaluation of atrial fibrillation.
3. Patient instructed to seek immediate medical attention if he experiences new palpitations or chest pain.

Electronically signed,
L. Moreau, PA-C
May 14, 2026
explanations: Atrial fibrillation cured by ablation, with no recurrence and no treatment: personal history, Z86.79 (no HCC).

distractors.why: It no longer exists and is not treated: code the history, not current AF.
